images.title: Count the hops
images.purpose: Show that going from 5 to 9 along the number line is 4 hops, counting the hops and not the stones.
images.composition: One horizontal row of stepping stones across the middle with 4 arcs above it and one label below, much white space around.
images.exact_structure: One horizontal row of 5 equal round stones in grey #6B7280 outline, evenly spaced, numbered 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 from left to right; the first stone teal #0072B2 and the last stone amber #E69F00. Above the row, exactly 4 equal arcs in reddish purple #CC79A7, one between each pair of neighbouring stones, all pointing right. Exactly 5 stones, 4 arcs.

images.takeaway: Count the hops between the stones, not the stones.
images.description: Five numbered stones from 5 to 9 with 4 arcs between neighbouring stones, showing 4 steps.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the arcs aloud, then say why the first stone is not counted.

image_decisions.why: Hops versus stones is a picture idea; one row of stones with 4 arcs carries it.
